plaintext.title: Response received over plain HTTP
plaintext.rationale: Anyone on the network path can read or alter this traffic.
plaintext.reference: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

plaintext-credentials.title: Credentials sent over plain HTTP
plaintext-credentials.rationale: The credential travelled unencrypted and can be captured on the network path.
plaintext-credentials.reference: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

https-downgrade.title: Redirect moved the exchange to plain HTTP
https-downgrade.rationale: A server sent an encrypted request on to an unencrypted URL; what follows can be read or altered on the network path.
https-downgrade.reference: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet; RFC 6797

verification-disabled.title: Certificate verification is turned off
verification-disabled.rationale: The server's identity was not checked; an impostor would have been accepted.

untrusted-certificate.title: Server certificate is not trusted
untrusted-certificate.rationale: The certificate failed verification; the connection went ahead only because verification is off.

legacy-protocol.title: Legacy TLS protocol negotiated
legacy-protocol.rationale: Versions older than TLS 1.2 are deprecated and have known weaknesses.

non-aead-cipher.title: Non-AEAD cipher negotiated
non-aead-cipher.rationale: CBC, RC4, 3DES and NULL ciphers lack authenticated encryption and have practical attacks.

no-forward-secrecy.title: No forward secrecy
no-forward-secrecy.rationale: A static RSA key exchange lets anyone who later obtains the server's key decrypt recorded traffic.

certificate-expired.title: Server certificate has expired
certificate-expired.rationale: Clients that verify certificates refuse this connection.

certificate-expiring.title: Server certificate expires soon
certificate-expiring.rationale: Renew it before clients start refusing the connection.

weak-key.title: Weak certificate key
weak-key.rationale: RSA and DSA keys under 2048 bits, and EC keys under 256 bits, are below current minimums.

hsts-missing.title: Strict-Transport-Security is missing
hsts-missing.rationale: Browsers may fall back to plain HTTP on a later visit.

hsts-short-max-age.title: Strict-Transport-Security max-age is short
hsts-short-max-age.rationale: A max-age under 180 days leaves a window in which browsers forget the policy.
hsts-short-max-age.reference: RFC 6797 §6.1.1; OWASP HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet

nosniff-missing.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is missing
nosniff-missing.rationale: Browsers may guess a different content type than the one declared.

csp-missing.title: Content-Security-Policy is missing
csp-missing.rationale: Without a policy, an injected script runs with the page's full privileges.

frame-protection-missing.title: No framing protection
frame-protection-missing.rationale: Another site can embed the page, which enables clickjacking.

cors-wildcard-credentials.title: Wildcard CORS with credentials
cors-wildcard-credentials.rationale: Allow-Origin * together with Allow-Credentials true is a contradiction browsers reject; it signals an over-broad policy.

cors-reflected-origin.title: CORS reflects the request Origin with credentials
cors-reflected-origin.rationale: Echoing any Origin with credentials lets any site read authenticated responses.
cors-reflected-origin.reference: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

cors-null-origin.title: CORS allows the null origin
cors-null-origin.rationale: Sandboxed documents and some redirects carry the null origin, so allowing it allows any site that can produce it.
cors-null-origin.reference: WHATWG Fetch Standard (CORS protocol); OWASP Web Security Testing Guide: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

version-disclosure.title: Server software version disclosed
version-disclosure.rationale: Version banners help match the server against known vulnerabilities.
version-disclosure.reference: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide: Fingerprint Web Server

missing-secure.title: Cookie set without Secure
missing-secure.rationale: Without the Secure attribute the browser also sends it over plain HTTP.

missing-httponly.title: Cookie set without HttpOnly
missing-httponly.rationale: Page scripts can read it, so an injected script could steal it.

credentials-in-query.title: Credential in the query string
credentials-in-query.rationale: URLs end up in logs, browser history and Referer headers.

sensitive-cacheable.title: Authenticated response may be cached
sensitive-cacheable.rationale: Without no-store or private, a shared cache may keep it and serve it to others.

set-cookie-cacheable.title: Response that sets a cookie is cacheable by shared caches
set-cookie-cacheable.rationale: A shared cache may store the response, Set-Cookie included, and hand one user's cookie to others.

setup.title: Save your workspace key
setup.intro: This key encrypts your secret variables. Every teammate and every other machine needs it to decrypt them.

rotate.warnNoRevoke: Rotating the workspace key does NOT revoke anyone who already had access — they may still know the secret values. To truly revoke access, rotate the underlying credentials at their providers.

gitNote.body: Encrypting protects this value from now on. Plaintext copies already in your Git history are not removed — if the value was ever pushed, rotate the credential at its provider.
